title: AI giants promise to play nice with personal data after UK watchdog scrutiny
key_facts: On Thursday (8 Oct 2026) the UK ICO said Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Stability AI have made or committed to changes after it examined their compliance with UK data protection law.
Changes include clearer explanations of how personal data trains models, better ways for people to exercise data rights, and tougher assessments of safeguards.
The supervisory programme began in 2025 with 11 developers; xAI was paused so the ICO could run a separate formal investigation into Grok.
The ICO admits current AI training practices still pose problems under UK data protection law, including personal data buried in models and removing data after training.
The ICO is monitoring whether developers deliver; some issues need industry, regulators and government to cooperate.
quote_evidence: Ten of the world's biggest AI developers have agreed to tighten their handling of personal data following scrutiny by Britain's privacy watchdog
The watchdog isn't declaring victory just yet.
That number dropped to ten after the ICO paused its engagement with Elon Musk's xAI to pursue a separate formal investigation into its Grok chatbot.
why_it_matters_hint: Ten major developers promised better handling of personal data, but the regulator says real problems remain and it has no proof yet that promises will be kept.
notes: The ICO's own announcement was not opened; read through The Register. The Register calls it the 'Information Commission's Office'; the entry uses 'ICO'. Overlaps with C12-05 (same announcement, agents angle).
